narrative.summary: During a cold winter at Halloway Manor, Cecil Thorne is found stabbed in his locked study. The room appears sealed with no signs of forced entry or exit. Suspicion falls on circus troupe members wintering on the estate, especially Ivor Yardley, recently threatened with eviction. However, Adela Halloway uncovers that a concealed rotating wall panel created a hidden access, enabling the killer to enter and leave unseen. The murderer is revealed to be Harriet Bellamy, the housekeeper, who resented the circus disrupting manor routines.

accepted_facts: Cecil Thorne was found stabbed with a letter opener in his locked study.
The study door and windows were locked from inside with no forced entry.
A heavy stone wall panel in the study conceals a hidden rotating doorway.
The letter opener was kept in the library by Adela Halloway.
The letter opener has a glove mark found in the library belonging to Marguerite Selwyn.
Harriet Bellamy’s alibi covers the apparent time of death but not the actual time.
Ivor Yardley was rehearsing in the stables at the murder time window.
Ottoline Fairweather was in the drawing room during the murder time.
Adela Halloway discovered wear marks on the carpet near the rotating panel.
inferred_conclusions: The rotating wall panel was used to enter and exit the study unseen.
The letter opener’s glove mark misdirects suspicion towards Marguerite Selwyn.
Harriet Bellamy’s alibi fails to cover the actual murder time.
Harriet Bellamy disturbed the letter opener while committing the murder.
The circus members have alibis during the actual time of death.
Only Harriet Bellamy had both motive and access to the hidden panel.

mechanism.description: A large stone wall panel in Cecil Thorne’s study is mounted on a concealed pivot under a thick carpet. This panel rotates to reveal a hidden doorway connecting to the servants’ corridor. The panel’s rotation allows the murderer to enter and leave the locked room without unlocking the main door or windows, creating the illusion of an impossible locked-room murder.

delivery_path.step: Murderer uses knowledge of hidden panel to enter study via servants’ corridor.
Kills Cecil Thorne with letter opener.
Rotates panel back to conceal doorway, restoring appearance of solid wall.
Returns letter opener to library, leaving glove mark of innocent suspect as misdirection.

outcome.result: The rotating wall panel conceals the killer’s entry and exit route, disproving the assumption that the study was sealed. The letter opener’s glove mark planted a red herring. Harriet Bellamy’s incomplete alibi and disturbance of the weapon prove her guilt.

false_assumption.statement: The study was completely sealed with no possible entrance or exit except the locked door and windows.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: All visible access points were locked from inside with no signs of forced entry or exit; the heavy stone walls appeared solid and unbroken.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: A concealed rotating stone wall panel creates a hidden doorway allowing secret access.

false_solution.the_one_flaw: The study’s locked windows and door exclude entry by Ivor, and he has a solid alibi for the actual time of death.

discriminating_test.design: A controlled demonstration rotates the suspected wall panel while the study door and windows remain locked, proving secret access. The letter opener is traced from the library to the servants’ corridor, confirming Harriet Bellamy’s manipulation. The test confirms only Harriet had knowledge and opportunity to use the rotating panel.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The rotating wall panel’s existence and use, the letter opener’s handling marks, and Harriet Bellamy’s exclusive access to the servants’ corridor prove her guilt.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Harriet Bellamy cannot replicate the panel’s movement without revealing her knowledge; the letter opener’s handling marks align exclusively with her access.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1: The glove mark on the letter opener (early) exonerates Marguerite Selwyn. Step 2: The handling mark in the servants’ corridor (early) implicates Harriet Bellamy’s presence with the weapon. Step 3: Wear marks on the carpet near the rotating panel (mid) reveal the hidden access. Step 4: Harriet Bellamy’s alibi gap (mid) places her at the murder time. These clues enable the reader to deduce the rotating panel mechanism and identify Harriet as the culprit before the discriminating test.
